scientific_claim: none; all wall-clock numbers produced by the two concurrent jobs are DISCARDED as evidence
what_happened: Job A (ThE3rS, PID 27348) was started 2026-11-13T23:37:13Z with the pre-review e3_e5_v1.py: latency --device cuda --batches 40 --repeats 3 --warmup 1. Its log reached config 9/37 at elapsed 1140.2 s.
Job B (jvgzz3, PID 15052) was started 2026-11-13T23:51:27Z with the reviewed e3_e5_v1.py: latency --device cuda --batches 40 --warmup 1 --repeats 3 --resume. It wrote 3 incremental config records.
Both jobs ran on the SAME local RTX 3060 from 23:51Z onward, violating the single-GPU-single-job constraint and contaminating matched wall-clock timing by GPU contention.

A too-narrow liveness filter at the start of the B session reported 0 python/conda processes while PID 27348 was in fact alive; the broader CommandLine query later exposed both job chains. The liveness-check limitation is recorded here, not hidden.
why_both_are_discarded: GPU contention makes median wall-clock non-matched and therefore unusable as E3/E5 latency evidence.
Job A additionally used the pre-review script that constructed frozen threshold tensors INSIDE every timed forward, adding mode-dependent non-forward overhead to the measurement.
Neither job produced e5_latency_v1.json; no latency number is treated as a result.
resolution: Quarantine the three artifacts here; terminate both job chains; verify GPU idle and zero e3_e5_v1.py processes; relaunch ONE clean job with the reviewed script, unchanged --batches 40 --warmup 1 --repeats 3, plus --resume for heartbeat-safe incremental evidence; publish the new job handle in GPU_QUEUE.md so no heartbeat restarts a duplicate.
constraints_unchanged: no shortened batches, no reduced repeats, no dropped timesteps, no threshold/scale/seed change, no protocol or frozen-hash edit
